wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are trying to orient themselves on the country, and one that tends to move when Iran becomes a party to something rather than a subject of it.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has drained steadily since mid-July even as the Strait of Hormuz dispute hardened: Trump said "We own it" of the strait and threatened to declare it US territory, Tehran called it an inseparable part of its territorial waters, US missiles crippled a cargo ship running the blockade, and the Guard Corps says it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper over Bandar Abbas. Readers are following the strait, not the country.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: The Strait of Hormuz has driven the window. Prices peaked in May and have fallen a fifth since, holding near the low even as Iran declared an indefinite blockade — Brent rose 12 cents on the news — and two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz. Talks between Iran, Oman and the US on reopening the strait have kept the war-risk premium contained.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, the US light sweet crude benchmark priced at Cushing, Oklahoma. It sets what American refiners pay, and petrol, diesel and freight costs follow it.
wti.recent: The barrel has given back a quarter of its value over the window despite a run of attacks on oil infrastructure: two ADNOC tankers struck transiting Hormuz, a third drone strike on Libya's Zawiya refinery, 12 missiles on Yemen's oil provinces and a drone attack on Nizhnekamsk deep inside Russia. Hopes of Hormuz reopening pulled prices back from the May high.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline junction and used to price most North American gas contracts. It drives what Americans pay to heat homes and run power plants, and it sets the floor for LNG sold abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The move is a drift down: gas fell from $3.34 on May 29 to a low of $2.56 on Aug 7, ending at $2.79. US demand headlines point the other way — SpaceX is building its own gas power plants for a Texas chip factory rather than wait on the grid, and Amazon is funding a 35-turbine plant at Fort Stockton.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. Its level sets the cost of bread and flour across importing countries, and governments that subsidise the loaf carry the difference on their own budgets.
wheat.recent: Prices have risen through the summer as war and drought hit the supply chain at once: Russia set Izmail, Ukraine's largest Danube grain port, ablaze and struck its rail station, while drought across Europe ran the Danube low enough to shut a reactor at Cernavoda. The FAO's food price index reached 131.1.

rice.standing: The benchmark export price for a tonne of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the world's population. It is thinly traded relative to wheat or maize, so export bans by a single large supplier can move it sharply.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen against a wider food-price rise: the Food and Agriculture Organization's index hit 131.1, a three-year high driven by heatwaves and wars pushing up crop costs, while diesel at $5.36 a gallon added freight cost to other staples. A record El Nino threatens 49 million with acute hunger in southern Africa.

copper.standing: The world benchmark price for refined copper, quoted per tonne. Copper is the metal grids, motors and buildings are wired with, so its price tracks electrification and construction demand and feeds through to the cost of everything that carries current.
copper.recent: Copper has run to a record 13,550 $/mt in June 2026, half again above its December 2024 low of 8,910. The demand side is visible in the grid build-out — Texas halted new data centre grid connections with 474 gigawatts of requests queued, five times peak demand — while supply stays slow to answer: the Mes Aynak deal signed in 2008 has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the benchmark price of borrowing for the world's largest borrower. It sets the floor under mortgages, corporate credit and sovereign spreads everywhere, and moves on inflation, Fed policy and demand for Treasuries.
us-10y.recent: The yield sat near the top of its range after the BOJ held rates at 1% on 31 July while warning underlying inflation was running above its 2% target, the same day the series peaked at 4.75%. Since then the dollar fell to its weakest since May as a rate hike came into doubt, and Trump again moved to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

sp500.standing: The main US equity benchmark, tracking 500 large listed companies weighted by market value, and the index most of the world's passive retirement money is invested against. Membership is decided by a committee, not a formula.
sp500.recent: Reddit rose 11% on the S&P Dow Jones Indices committee's decision alone, with inclusion set for August 18 — no earnings changed, but every fund tracking the index must buy before then. The series peaked at 7799 on Aug 13, up 5.17% over the window, with stocks gaining earlier in the month on Hormuz reopening hopes.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is the most concentrated public bet on large-cap technology, so chip, cloud and consumer-device earnings move it more than the broad market.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its two-month range after a run of hardware and AI capital news: Nvidia arranged $500 billion in financing through six lenders for buyers of its chips, Amazon backed a Texas gas plant to power a datacentre, and Apple's China-only AI model was cleared by regulators in Beijing.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude oil with a lag but adds refining margins, taxes and regional bottlenecks, and it is the most visible price in US consumer inflation.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining capacity, not crude, has driven the swing: Ukrainian drones hit two Russian refineries on 6 August and killed 13 at Nizhnekamsk on 10 August, while a third drone strike set Libya's Zawiya refinery alight and a fire struck Aramco's Jizan facility. Yet export margins have collapsed enough that India cut its windfall levy on petrol exports to nil.

natgas-ttf.standing: The benchmark price for wholesale natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub. It prices heating, electricity and the fertiliser and chemicals industries across the continent, and it moves on pipeline supply, LNG cargo competition and weather.
natgas-ttf.recent: The input does not explain the move. European gas rose about 24% across the window, to $15.09/MMBtu, well above December's $9.46 low and short of the $17.67 March peak.

vix.standing: A CBOE index of expected S&P 500 volatility over the coming 30 days, derived from options prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of how much stress the market is pricing.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down through the summer to sit just off its 64-day low of 14.55 on Aug 12, well below the 22.22 reached on Jun 10. The same calm shows up elsewhere: bitcoin volatility nearly vanished as ETFs took in $754 million, and traders read the sell-off from $65,000 as thin volume rather than panic.

fx-pkr.standing: The exchange rate of Pakistan's currency against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and much of its food, so the rate sets the domestic price of both, and it governs the local cost of servicing dollar debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat over the month, moving in a band between 276.6 on Jul 31 and 278.2 on Jul 22 to sit at 277.6. The stability held through a fuel-price shock — diesel at 383.95 rupees a litre after a Hormuz war-risk levy — and a dealer-margin strike that was settled rather than allowed to run.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate between Nigeria's naira and the US dollar. Nigeria is Africa's largest oil exporter and imports most of its fuel and food, so the naira sets domestic prices for both and transmits every shift in oil revenue into household costs.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira held a narrow band, easing from 1,381 on Jul 22 to 1,358 on Jul 31 before settling near 1,360. Abuja is forgoing tax revenue to unlock $50 billion in deep offshore oil investment against declining output, while the Senate pressed Seplat Energy over a skipped audit hearing. Osun's election drew 34 incidents and 18 deaths before Saturday's vote.

fx-egp.standing: The Egyptian pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat, fuel and medicine, so the rate sets the domestic price of essentials and the cost of servicing the state's foreign-currency debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound traded in a narrow band, from 51.37 on Jul 25 to 49.56 on Aug 8, ending near 50.06. Nothing in the period explains a move of that size; the currency's weight showed up instead at the pharmacy counter, where a drug pricing freeze held against a devaluation has emptied shelves.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar so a rising number means a weaker lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and much of its food, so the rate feeds straight into domestic prices and into the cost of servicing foreign-currency debt.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a 30-day low of 47.88 on Aug 14, roughly 1.5 percent weaker across the month, a slow grind rather than a break. Nothing in the month's Turkish news explains it: the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, the Kurdish disarmament law and the Bosphorus passage rationing all passed without a visible mark on the rate.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's currency against the US dollar. Bangladesh imports most of its fuel, food grain and industrial inputs and earns dollars mainly from garment exports and remittances, so the rate sets the price of both.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, set daily in a market that prices Southeast Asia's largest economy. Indonesia imports fuel and much of its food, so a weaker rupiah raises domestic prices before it shows up anywhere else.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah is roughly where it started the month, having drifted from 18,110 on Jul 28 to 17,800 on Aug 8 and back to 17,830. The one move the reporting explains is the small rise after Prabowo named a central bank deputy as his nominee for governor on Aug 11 — a succession question the market had been holding open.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Since the 2019 banking collapse it has traded far below its old peg, and because Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine, the rate sets the price of nearly everything sold there.
fx-lbp.recent: The rate has barely moved, drifting between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7 — a range of well under one percent — even as the truce with Israel frayed. Strikes continued through the seventh round of direct talks in Rome, and an attack near Ansar killed seven on Aug 15. The currency has absorbed none of it.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted as yuan per US dollar, and the price at which the world's largest exporter's goods are converted into dollars. Beijing manages its daily trading band, so its moves read as policy as much as market.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted stronger across the month, from 6.775 on Jul 18 to 6.743 on Aug 15, a move of under half a percent. Nothing in the period's China news — Zhu Rongji's death at 97, Apple's cleared home-grown model, the US accusing China of evading tariffs — accounts for a move that small.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's exchange rate against the US dollar. India imports most of its crude, so a weaker rupee raises the landed cost of fuel and fertiliser, and it sets the value of the remittances sent home by one of the world's largest migrant workforces.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has firmed about 1% over the month, from 96.65 on Jul 18 to 95.61, touching 95.05 on Aug 5. Cheaper crude helped: one remark on Iran cut oil 4.5% in early August. Retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, and New Delhi cut petrol's export tax from ₹3.5 to nil.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate between Brazil's real and the US dollar, and the price at which Latin America's largest economy trades. It swings on commodity earnings, the central bank's policy rate and domestic politics, and it sets the local cost of imported fuel, machinery and debt.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened through a month of political friction: Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador, tying its restoration to Brasília accepting its own envoy pick, and the Workers' Party nominated Lula da Silva for a fourth presidential term with no successor in place. The currency hit its weakest point of the window on Aug 15.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends the large majority of its exports to the United States, so the rate carries every shift in trade policy and cross-border politics.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened through a month of friction with Washington rather than despite it: the US put a $25 million bounty on a Sinaloa Cartel leader on 5 August, then cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum. Mexico also restored diplomatic relations with Peru. None of it dented the currency.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, the most traded currency pair in the world. It moves on the gap between what the European Central Bank and the Federal Reserve do with interest rates, and it sets the import price of energy and food for 350 million people.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted down about 1.1 percent over the month from its 26 July high to 0.8643 on 15 August. Nothing in the European news of the period explains it: the run of stories was regulatory and domestic — an EU sourcing law in draft, France's court striking down its under-15 social media ban, jellyfish shutting three nuclear reactors at Gravelines.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, quoted as yen per dollar, and one of the world's most traded. A weak yen inflates the earnings Japanese exporters bring home and raises the cost of the fuel and food the country imports.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen's strongest point in the window followed a joint US-Japan intervention confirmed on 3 August, which pushed the dollar to a one-month low and reversed the slide from 163.9 on 26 July. It has since drifted back toward 159.3. Toyota, reporting quarterly profit of $9.4 billion, was among the exporters banking the cheap-yen windfall.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker ruble. Sanctioned out of most Western markets, it now trades chiefly on oil receipts, capital controls and war news.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid to 84.18 on Aug 15 from 77.69 on Jul 25 as strikes hit the export and industrial base behind it: Ukraine struck the Samara rocket plant and the port of Novorossiysk, drones burned nearly $2 billion of Wildberries stock, and Russia hit the Danube grain port of Izmail. Lavrov rejected freezing the war at the current front line.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, priced against the dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It carries the country's mining exports and its politics, and moves on both commodity demand and the state of domestic institutions.
fx-zar.recent: The rand strengthened from 16.83 on 25 July to 16.15 on 8 August, its floor for the month, before settling at 16.17. The domestic news in this window ran to policing and procurement — soldiers deployed in Cape Town where 70 people were killed in a week, and the Prasa security-contract investigation in Pretoria — rather than to anything that would move the currency itself.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency, set on exchanges that trade around the clock. It has no issuer and no yield, so its price is pure demand — and it sets the tone for every other crypto asset.
btc.recent: The Coldcard exploit did the damage: attackers drained $120 million from self-custody wallets, the attack spread to 4,500 addresses, and holders sent bitcoin back to exchanges rather than hold their own keys. Bitcoin slipped under $63,000 on 3 August as the exploit entered a fifth day, and it has not recovered since.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, and the settlement layer most tokens, stablecoins and decentralised exchanges are built on. Its price is a rough gauge of how much capital is committed to on-chain finance.
eth.recent: The month tracked a sector consolidating rather than expanding: over 100 crypto projects folded in 2026, and of the $11.2 billion raised in six months, none went permissionless — capital bought regulatory licences instead. Prices declined in early August as the Coldcard exploit entered a fifth day, then recovered as the sweeps receded.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by physical gold in a London vault, tracking the metal's dollar price per ounce. It trades continuously on crypto exchanges, so it prices gold on nights and weekends when the bullion market is shut.
paxg.recent: Gold climbed toward a ten-week high through mid-August as buyers positioned ahead of US inflation data, with spot gold at $4,392 an ounce on Wednesday 12 August. The token's own peak came a day later, alongside KPMG's Tether audit, which counted the stablecoin issuer's gold bars by hand.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day — a rough gauge of how far interest in the technology has spread beyond the people who build it, rather than a measure of the technology itself.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership climbed to its 13 August peak alongside a run of stories about AI's reach into ordinary work and institutions: Commure ending referral payments to doctors, a Hartford legal filing with invisible text instructing AI models to side with the plaintiff, Anthropic extending watermarking to text Claude only edits, and Seoul staking $880 billion on chips and power.

wiki-russia.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Russia — a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to understand the country at any given moment, and one that tracks wars, elections and crises rather than anything about Russia itself.
wiki-russia.recent: The rise tracked strikes running both directions. A Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk killed at least 13 deep inside Russia on 10 August, and drones hit Novorossiysk naval base and port on 12 August; Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and hit the Danube grain port of Izmail. Lavrov rejected freezing the war at the current front line.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Wikipedia's Pakistan article, and how many people open it each day. It is a rough gauge of outside curiosity about a nuclear-armed state of some 250 million people, and it moves when the country enters someone else's news cycle.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The late-July peak followed the Mecca defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, which analysts began describing as a 'Sunni NATO' and which now binds defence chiefs and foreign ministers into a standing bloc. Attention has since eased as the story moved to Yemen and the Houthi strikes.

wiki-china.standing: Pageviews of the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how many people are looking the country up on any given day, and one that rises when China enters a story most readers do not already have the background for.
wiki-china.recent: Zhu Rongji, the former premier whose restructuring cost tens of millions of jobs and carried China into the WTO, died on 12 August at 97 — the day before the peak. The same week Beijing tightened drone exports as America accused China of evading tariffs, Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan, and Jakarta signed onto China's Taiwan language.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman linking the Gulf to the Indian Ocean, and the route roughly a fifth of the world's oil takes to market. It has no alternative at scale, so any threat to passage prices into crude, freight and insurance worldwide.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracks a strait that is closed and being bargained over. Iran has kept Hormuz shut behind six conditions and a reparations demand, with 8 to 15 ships crossing daily; Trump declared "We own it," a claim Tehran rejects. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting, and the Guard Corps says it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: Bitcoin is the first and largest cryptocurrency, secured by miners who spend electricity to validate transactions. Its price, its security model and its power appetite make it a proxy for the whole crypto market and a live question for grids.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Readership tracked a run of security failures rather than a price move: a Coldcard hack drained $120 million and congested the mempool with the attacker's own transactions, a Toronto hardware-wallet maker destroyed inventory after thieves stole $88 million through a firmware bug, and attackers drained Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes. An audit by sixteen developers filed 4,962 findings in a day.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia each day. It rises when the kingdom is at the centre of a story, and tracks general curiosity rather than markets or policy.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Three states signed a collective-defence pact at Mecca on Friday, and Egypt stayed out; the deal names no obligations and never states whose nuclear deterrent applies. Houthi missiles then hit Marib and Najran, wounding 11 including a 4-year-old, and Yemen said its forces struck a Saudi military site.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the sitting US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with what the presidency is doing, making it a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention Washington is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership has drifted down through August after the July peak. The stories driving traffic since have been episodic rather than singular: the halted attack on Iran and the claim that the US fully controls the Strait of Hormuz, then the disclosure that Trump left Ankara hidden inside a catering truck.

wiki-india.standing: The Wikipedia article on India, one of the most-read country pages on the site. Its daily readership rises when the country is in the world's news, so the curve works as a rough gauge of global attention on a nation of over a billion people.
wiki-india.recent: Readership climbed into mid-August around the 80th Independence Day and Modi's Red Fort address, where he promised up to eight more semiconductor plants, five nuclear reactors by 2030 and 100GW of nuclear capacity by 2047, alongside an offshore push into previously 'no-go' maritime blocks. An Army band opened the ceremony with Vande Mataram.

wiki-israel.standing: Wikipedia's page for Israel, and how many people open it each day. Attention to a country's encyclopaedia entry rises when readers meet its name somewhere else first, so the curve tracks what a general audience is trying to place in context.
wiki-israel.recent: Readership climbed toward the 11 August peak as Israel's West Bank operations broadened, with more than 500 attacks recorded in a week and a new checkpoint erected near Ni'lin, and as Venezuela restored consular ties after 17 years. Israeli strikes on south Lebanon and demolitions around Mansouri ran through the same window.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country rather than reading the day's headlines about it.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Attention has drifted down through August even as the war widened: Ukrainian drones killed 13 in Nizhnekamsk on 10 August, 1,600 km from the border, and struck the Novorossiysk naval base on 12 August, while Russia set Izmail's Danube grain port ablaze and hit Odessa's export terminals.

wiki-nigeria.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria — Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. Readership rises when the country's politics, security or energy sector break into the wider news.
wiki-nigeria.recent: The peak fell around the Osun state election, where a violence tracker logged 34 incidents and 18 deaths before Saturday's vote and Tinubu ordered the EFCC to vacate a freeze on the Osun account. Aviation unions then struck, barricading Air Peace terminals in Lagos, and AFRICOM strikes in West Africa drew a rebuke from the Sahel bloc.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to a handful of vessels a day under Iran's blockade, with tankers that do sail exposed: two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz on 13 August, and US Hellfire missiles crippled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. Iran says 8 to 15 ships now cross daily, and reopening stays conditional while Trump claims Washington owns the strait.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic has fallen with the Houthi campaign along both shores. A projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, missiles and drones hit the Red Sea port of Mokha, and six sailors died in a strike on a cargo ship. Maersk, rerouting around the closure, raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic recovered from a 21-vessel trough on Jun 16 to 48 a day, but stayed only marginally above its 90-day baseline as attacks on the southern approach continued: six sailors died in a Bab al-Mandeb strike on a cargo ship, and a projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel. Maersk, still routing around the Red Sea, raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has stayed close to its own 90-day baseline despite disruption at the other end of the route: the Hormuz closure has cut Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia, with Hormuz vessel transits falling to a fraction of normal, and Malaysian refineries turning to substitute barrels. Seas through the strait were calm, with waves under a metre.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic runs about 15% below its 90-day baseline, with a swing from 28 vessels on Jul 10 to 401 on Jul 12. Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan, and China braced for Typhoon Dolphin with flight cancellations and evacuations on 2026-08-09 — the storm window sits alongside the latest reading of 232.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Traffic has fallen through a drought-heavy summer: the count peaked at 83 vessels on Jul 13, collapsed to 22 by Jul 22, and now sits at 29, about 4% below its 90-day baseline. The input does not name a Panama-specific cause; the same season has run rivers low from the Rhine at Nijmegen to the Danube at Cernavoda.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has thinned as the war moved onto the water. Turkey turned back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk, TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, and a drone killed a crewman on a Turkish-owned coal hauler — with Ukraine striking Novorossiysk itself on 12 August. Grain and oil out of Odesa carry the cost.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic sits near the low end of its 84-day range, and the input does not explain why. The strait's own crossings have been in the news for people rather than cargo: nearly 60,000 swam from Morocco into Ceuta in a week, and 72,000 crossed into a city of 84,000.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has run close to its own 90-day baseline, with the low of 126 vessels on Aug 3 and no weather alert on the water. The strait's other traffic dominated the news: a dinghy carrying about 160 people caught fire off Boulogne-sur-Mer on Aug 4, and Western Europe recorded its hottest June and July.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has drifted down through the window, from 123 vessels on 31 July to 83, about 6% below the 90-day baseline. Nothing in the record explains the fall — the tanker attacks reported near Hormuz and off Oman sit on the routes this detour exists to avoid, and Maersk lifted its full-year profit guidance to $6.5bn over the same period.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, some 98 percent below its own 90-day baseline, after months in which the Black Sea became a shooting gallery: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, Ukraine hit the Russian port of Novorossiysk in a drone strike, and Putin threatened from a warship to seize cargo ships in retaliation.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits below its mid-June level after weeks of Houthi fire reaching Saudi soil: strikes wounded 11 civilians in Najran, a claimed attack on the Jazan refinery that processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily, and a fire Aramco says was extinguished at its Jizan facility. Riyadh signed the Mecca defence pact with Turkiye and Pakistan on 7 August but has not retaliated.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits below its 18 June high after a crowded fortnight for Ankara: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca on 7 August, parliament passed a law on Kurdish disarmament on 10 August, and Moscow protested a US-Turkey arms transfer to Ukraine. Turkey also rationed Bosphorus passage, turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after a violent security month: seven blasts hit Jebel Ali port on 5 August, two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz, and Iran pressed new demands around the strait. Against that, construction began on the Abu Dhabi-Dubai high-speed rail line.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 5 high of 1748 as the Hormuz closure reached Malaysian refineries, cutting Gulf crude arrivals to a fraction of normal volumes and forcing import substitution. Domestic politics added to the drag: Anwar Ibrahim's coalition lost Negeri Sembilan to a Malay-nationalist wave, and the DAP scheduled a vote on staying in the unity government.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index sits below where it started the window after a June trough, with monetary leadership the live question: Prabowo nominated a Bank Indonesia deputy as the new governor, and the rupiah rose slightly on the news. Jakarta has also drawn attention abroad, signing a communique endorsing China's position on Taiwan.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: A weak yen carried exporter earnings: Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion on the cheap currency in early August. The joint US-Japan intervention on 3 August, which pushed the dollar to a one-month low, cut against that, and the index sits well below its 25 June high.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has drifted down through the window from its May 14 high of 26,390 to 25,120, with a 1.1% fall on the day, near the low of 22,670 set on Jun 26. The coverage does not name a market-moving event behind the slide.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits about 6% below its mid-May peak of 4,178, having bottomed at 3,764 on 17 July before a partial recovery to 3,927. Nothing in the record explains the drift.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen 12.57% across the window, from 9115 on Jun 22 to a low of 5594 on Jul 30, with the slide running through Korea's $880 billion AI and memory build-out — SK Hynix dropped 5% on its $38 billion fab bet even as all 2027 memory capacity sold out. North Korea's missile launches ahead of US-South Korea drills, and Lee's call for talks to end the war, framed the recovery to 6978.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index has climbed roughly 3 per cent over the window, peaking on Aug 6 before easing. New Delhi has spent the period reshaping the terms companies operate on: petrol's export tax cut from ₹3.5 to nil, a mineral tax bill stripping states of mining royalties, and eight more chip plants promised. In Mumbai, Tata Trusts moved to name a successor at India's biggest conglomerate.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has gained about 15 percent over the past two months, reaching a high of 5,754 on Aug 11 before easing slightly. The input does not explain what drove the run.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 22 high of 47740 after bottoming at 39930 on Jul 30, with pressure from the strait rather than the fabs: Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan, and Jakarta signed a joint statement whose Taiwan language goes further than its own long-standing position.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits at the top of its 45-day range, having climbed steadily from the May low, and the domestic news of the period left no mark on it: a school shooting in Nonthaburi that killed eight and wounded 15, and Bangkok's decision to host Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing, moved politics rather than prices.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing off a late-May low, but slipped on the day. Manila's politics have run through the period: the Sara Duterte impeachment trial reached Day 14 with confidential-fund disbursements logged to unusual names and zero results, and a magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on 5 August.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the high it set on Aug 6, having climbed roughly a twentieth over the window, though it slipped on the latest session. The RBA held its cash rate steady on Aug 11 as the housing market softened, and China's steel stock has aged enough to recycle — a shift toward scrap that skips Australian iron ore, the index's largest export earner.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has drifted about 2.8% lower over the past nine weeks, from a 7 August high of 117,500 back toward 114,100, with the low of 108,300 set on 23 July. Nothing in the available material accounts for the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index has drifted to a 66-day low of 166,900, down 6.4% from its 178,400 peak on May 14. Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on August 4, saying it would restore it only if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick, and Lula was nominated for a fourth term on August 2.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down through a run of US friction with Mexico City: Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum, and offered $25 million for a Mexican cartel leader. A screwworm outbreak passing 500 human cases adds a hit to the livestock trade.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has climbed roughly 7% over the window, reaching its high of 36,760 on Aug 13, and has been effectively flat since. The input does not identify what drove the rise.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index set a high of 7799 on Aug 13 before easing 0.17%, up roughly 5% across the window from its Jun 10 low of 7267. The clearest single move in the coverage was Reddit's 11% jump on the S&P Dow Jones Indices committee's decision to add it — every fund tracking the index must buy the stock before 18 August.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index is up about 3.6% over the window, peaking at 10,910 on Jul 29 before easing to 10,750. Nothing in this period's UK news explains the drift: the domestic stories were political and local — Nigel Farage reclaiming the Clacton parliamentary seat on 14 August, and a Southern train derailment at Lewes, East Sussex.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached its highest level of the period on Aug 14, up roughly 8% since May. Bank shares had support from Commerzbank saying a tie-up with UniCredit could create value, a deal Berlin had previously called a sovereignty threat. Little else in the window points at Frankfurt directly.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index reached 8,726 on Aug 10 and has drifted since, ending at 8,637. The domestic news in the window was not market-moving: France's top court struck down the under-15 social media ban, and jellyfish swarms shut three nuclear reactors, knocking out 3.2 gigawatts. Nothing here explains the drift.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index climbed through the period to a high of 1120 on Aug 13, up roughly nine percent over the window, before easing slightly. Shell agreed to sell its European onshore renewables business on Aug 3, the one corporate move in the window at that scale. Nothing else in the record explains the rise.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index reached 20,210 on 11 August, near the top of a run of roughly 13% since a 17,620 low on 15 May. Nothing in the Spanish news of the period explains the climb: the domestic stories were the Ceuta crossings, where 72,000 people entered a city of 84,000, and reciprocal border checks with Italy — neither of which touched the listed banks and utilities that dominate the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, having climbed roughly 7% from its 19 May low of 48,360 to a 7 August high of 53,720. Nothing in the record explains the run: the Italian news of the period was Spain's reciprocal border checks, the resignation of three directors at the space agency, and Milan-based Bending Spoons buying Airtable for $1.28bn.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, up about 9% over the window and roughly a fifth of a percent below the 14,630 high set on Aug 10, after a low of 13,220 on Jun 3. The available material does not explain what drove the climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after climbing roughly 8 percent from its 15 May low of 3036, peaking at 3327 on 5 Aug before easing. The coverage in this window does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-spain.standing: The Wikipedia article on Spain, and a daily count of how many people read it. Attention series like this one spike when a country hosts an event, a crisis or a spectacle that sends people looking for the basics.
wiki-spain.recent: Spain sat on the path of the total solar eclipse of 12 August, Europe's first in 30 years, with totality lasting 81 seconds at Teruel and under two minutes at Burgos. Readership has fallen back by half since, the low on 12 August itself. The Ceuta crossings, 72,000 people into a city of 84,000, ran alongside it.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the meeting after September. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for a hold — not a forecast, and it moves as the case for cutting or holding shifts.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract has moved with the fight over who controls the Fed: it sat at 39 on Aug 1, and Trump's renewed move to fire Cook on Aug 7, reviving the fight over Fed independence, sits inside the run up to 75 on Aug 15. Polymarket itself was in the news over the same weeks — JPMorgan's debanking, and a rules overhaul after a study found fraud.

wiki-turkey.standing: A count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on Turkey each day — a rough gauge of when a country stops being background and becomes something outsiders go looking up.
wiki-turkey.recent: Turkey signed a collective-defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on 7 August, described in coverage as a possible 'Sunni NATO', with Egypt absent and each state's commitments left undefined. Ankara then passed a Kurdish disarmament law on 10 August, and Moscow objected to US missiles reaching Ukraine via Turkey.

poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran extend their 60-day negotiating window. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each sign that the channel is holding or breaking.
poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.recent: The window narrowed as the confrontation widened. Trump said of the Strait of Hormuz "We own it," and Iran's judiciary chief answered that the strait cannot be seized by a tweet; the Guard Corps then said it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper over Hormozgan, and Iran declared an indefinite blockade.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel and Iran reach a ceasefire by a set date. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for it happening — a running read on how a war looks to those with money on it.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The price climbed from 26 on Jul 19 to 93 on Aug 15 as the Strait of Hormuz moved toward a deal: Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructure on Aug 2, and talks with Iran, Oman and the US were reported close and making progress. Strikes continued near Ansar and in Quneitra, but not enough to move the bet back.

poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Renan Santos wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it reads as a percentage and moves as money changes sides — a running tally of conviction rather than a poll.
poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.recent: Nothing in the record explains the slide. The contract peaked at 12 on Jul 25 and has drifted down since, touching 5 on Aug 16 — a loss of about half its value over the month.

xag.standing: A silver-backed digital token tracking the spot price of an ounce of silver. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input — it conducts better than any other element, which puts electronics and solar cells on the same price as the safe-haven bid.
xag.recent: The series more than doubled off its Aug 6 low of 29.80, reaching 66.52 on Aug 15 before easing to 65.17. A move of that size over nine days is not an ordinary repricing of the metal, and nothing in the window explains it.

stocks:RDDT.standing: Reddit is a US-listed social platform where users post to topic communities moderated by volunteers, and its revenue comes from advertising against that discussion and from licensing the archive to companies training language models.
stocks:RDDT.recent: Reddit rose 11% on 14 August after S&P Dow Jones Indices set its S&P 500 inclusion for 18 August — a committee decision, with no product or earnings change behind it. Every fund tracking the index must buy the stock before that date. Earlier in the window, Reddit's AI moderation wrongly deleted decade-old posts.

stocks:JPM.standing: One of the largest US banks, and a benchmark for the health of American credit and capital markets. Its shares move on rates, loan losses and trading revenue, and on what regulators allow banks to do.
stocks:JPM.recent: The stock drifted up through the window, from $338.90 on Jul 20 to a $365.20 high on Aug 12. Nothing in the period explains the move; the bank's own news was its relationship with Polymarket, which it debanked while continuing to court the firm.

stocks:AVB.standing: A US residential real estate investment trust that owns and operates large apartment portfolios, mostly in coastal metropolitan markets. Its shares trade on rent growth, occupancy and — like all REITs — the level of long-term interest rates.
stocks:AVB.recent: The series drifted down about 3% over three weeks, from $195.50 on Jul 16 to a low of $179.80 on Aug 12, with no event in the window accounting for the move.
